name: section1
label::English (en): Section 1: Assessor and Country information

name: email_assessor
label::English (en): Email address of assessor

name: name_assessor
label::English (en): Name of assessor

name: country_assessment
label::English (en): Country of assessment
hint::English (en): Please list the country for this specific assessment. Remember assessments are done for populations WITHIN the country of assessment, instead of the entire range of the species.

name: section2
label::English (en): Section 2: Species Taxonomy

name: genus
label::English (en): Genus

name: species
label::English (en): Species
hint::English (en): Only type the epithet, e.g. "sapiens" instead of "Homo sapiens". Do NOT include Taxonomic Authority or year of description. That will be provided below.
constraint_message: Only type the epithet, e.g. "sapiens" instead of "Homo sapiens"

name: note_species
label::English (en): While assessm ents are intended to be conducted at the species level, it is recognized that there are revisions of taxonomy, and what may be considered a subspecies or variety by some experts, may be considered a species by others. Also, distinctions at infraspecies levels may be of special importance for some taxa, like some crop wild relatives. Assessors may thus include subspecies or variety if the entity is an important unit for that country (e.g., it has separate management reports, protection level or Red List status or a wild relative of a crop).\_  See [Guidelines for the definition of subspecies, and issues of taxonomy](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/4\_Species\_list/Species\_list.html#on-the-definition-of-subspecies-and-issues-of-taxonomy)

name: subspecies_variety
label::English (en): Subspecies or Variety
hint::English (en): Only type the infraspecific epithet. Leave blank if the assessment is not being done below the species level.

name: scientific_authority
label::English (en): Taxonomic Authority
hint::English (en): Please include the Taxonomic Authority and year for the species (or subspecies/variety) being assessed. E.g., For Mellivora capensis, type (Schreber, 1776). If Unknown, please leave blank.

name: common_name
label::English (en): Common name
hint::English (en): Please provide the most widely used common name for the species, followed by the language in brackets. For example, the common names for Taxus baccata are Common yew in English and If commun in French. If more than one widely used common name exists, please separate them with a semicolon. E.g. Common yew (EN); If commun (FR).

name: taxonomic_group
label::English (en): Taxonomic Group

name: Taxonomic_Order
label::English (en): Taxonomic Order
hint::English (en): Please correctly type the Order this species belongs to, to assist with additional comparisons within a given taxonomic group.

name: note_taxonID
label::English (en): Taxon IDs can help form linkages between the different data sources, which may prove useful in downstream analyses or future projects. GBIF often provides several of these IDs known for the species at the bottom of the species page. If no IDs are available, please leave these questions blank.

name: GBIF_taxonID
label::English (en): If available, add the GBIF taxonID for this species
hint::English (en): e.g. 2684495 for Juniperus blancoi as shown here https://www.gbif.org/species/2684495 (scroll down to the end "Taxon identifiers" section.

name: NCBI_taxonID
label::English (en): If available, add the NCBI taxonID for this species
hint::English (en): e.g. 698470 for Juniperus blancoi as shown here https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/search/all/?term=juniperus%20blancoi

name: national_taxonID
label::English (en): If available, add the taxonID for this species from any information system or local database in the country of assessment.

name: source_national_taxonID
label::English (en): What's the name of the information system/local data base for the National taxonID you added before?

name: section3
label::English (en): Section 3: Proportion of maintained populations (PM indicator)

name: section3_note
label::English (en): **This section will directly help in quantifying the PM indicator, and will inform the section on Indicator 1 by stipulating the number of populations you will be asked to complete with respect to population name and size. For questions regarding [the reference period, please check the guidelines](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Reference\_period.html)**

name: note_pops1
label::English (en): The following questions are asking about the number of EXTINCT and EXTANT populations known within the country.

name: note_pops2
label::English (en): Please consult the [Gudelines on how populations can be defined](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Howto\_define\_populations.html). Examples for each method are provided. In there, you will also find information on metapopulations and how to quantify recently fragmented populations. If you are still uncertain, please pose your question on the [Google group](https://groups.google.com/g/genetic-indicators-project).

name: note_pops3
label::English (en): **Extinct** populations refer to the total number of known losses of historic populations in the country. Any population whose original gene pool in that location has disappeared entirely should be considered extinct. See the [guidelines for advice on how to find information on extinct populations](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Extinct\_extant\_populations.html)

name: n_extinct_populations
label::English (en): Number of EXTINCT (lost) populations within the country of assessment
hint::English (en): An integer count (e.g., 1, 2) must be reported. Type -999 if unknown
constraint_message: The number of extinct populations has to be >=0 or -999 if unknown

name: Did_you_mean_999
label::English (en): Did you mean -999 (unknown number of lost populations) instead of 999 in the previous question? Please change to -999

name: n_unassessed_populations
label::English (en): Are there any un-assessed populations within the country? (e.g. populations that we don't know if they are still there because we can't visit them). How many?

name: extinct_pop_names
label::English (en): Type the name or region of the extinct populations, separated by a semicolon (";")

name: note_npops
label::English (en): **IMPORTANT**: the number of populations entered in the next question will influence how many specific population sections appear in Section 5.

name: n_extant_populations
label::English (en): Number of EXTANT (still existing) populations within the country of assessment
hint::English (en): An integer count (e.g., 1, 2) must be reported. Type -999 if unknown
constraint_message: The number of extant populations has to be >=0 or -999 if unknown

name: Did_you_mean_999_001
label::English (en): Did you mean -999 (unknown number of populations) instead of 999 in the previous question? Please change to -999

name: time_populations
label::English (en): What year or time period is this population structure based on?
hint::English (en): I.e., the year of the report or database, or year of knowledge from local experts. Please only enter a single year or range of YYYY-YYYY

name: defined_populations
label::English (en): Broadly, which of the following categories better defines how populations are defined for this species? See [guidelines](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Howto\_define\_populations.html) for definitions and examples of each method. Note than more than one can be selected, if methods were combined.

name: source_definition_populations
label::English (en): Please provide a brief but clear explanation (method) on how populations were defined. See examples (figue legends) in the [How to define populations section of the guidelines](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Howto\_define\_populations.html)
hint::English (en): For example if a buffer zone among occurrence points was used, specify the source of the occurrence points and the size of the buffer: or if geographic layers (e.g. basins, biogeographic regions, etc) were used to crop the distribution range, please explain how was this done: or if it was based on expert consultation, please explain how (e.g. workshop, interview) and provide name of expert(s).

name: map_populations
label::English (en): If a map illustrating the extant populations exists, please upload it here, ensuring that each population is clearly marked. If only partial information on populations is available, it is highly recommended that assessors denote this information on the map(s) by indicating which populations are being assessed.
hint::English (en): A multipage document (eg pdf) can be included to "zoom in" into different populations, if required. Accepted files: pdf, png, jpg. Please be reasonable with file size.

name: source_populations
label::English (en): Source of species population information (literature reference, website link, expert consultation)
hint::English (en): Please list all relevant sources used in acquiring the species information separated by a semicolon (;). It is advised that all referenced documents are saved to a species specific folder in your personal records in case further consultation is required. If information was based on expert consultation, please provide name of expert(s).

name: diff_historical_pop
label::English (en): Do the number of HISTORICAL populations differ than what is currently EXTANT?

name: n_hist_pops
label::English (en): If yes, how many existed historically?
hint::English (en): An integer count (e.g., 1, 2) must be reported.

name: section4
label::English (en): Section 4: Preface to the Ne 500 indicator

name: note_section4
label::English (en): **These next questions will help quantify what population size data exists for populations of the species, and in doing so filter out unnecessary questions in Section 5. See guidelines for advice on [How to estimate population sizes (Nc or Ne)](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Populations\_sizes.html) **

name: note_section4b
label::English (en): In the following question ‘ANY DATA’ not only refers to quantitative data, but also qualitative and approximate/ imprecise data, or even an ability to confidently say the population is < Nc 5000. All data on population size can be useful and interpretable, even if only available for some populations.

name: popsize_data
label::English (en): Is there any data on population sizes (e.g. Ne, Nc) for at least ONE POPULATION for this species?

name: ne_pops_exists
label::English (en): Effective Size - Are there effective size estimates (Ne) from genetic data for at least one of the extant populations?
hint::English (en): See guidelines for [definition of Ne and how to obtain it](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Populations\_sizes.html#how-to-get-ne-from-genetic-studies)

name: nc_pops_exists
label::English (en): Census Size - Are there census size estimates (Nc) for at least one of the extant populations?
hint::English (en): See guidelines for [definition of Nc and how to obtain it](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Populations\_sizes.html#how-to-get-the-nc)

name: ratio_exists
label::English (en): Is there a known effective population size to census size (Ne/Nc) ratio for this species or a highly similar/closely [related species](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#closely-related-species) (e.g. within the same genus and having the same life history traits)?
hint::English (en): See [guidelines on How to get the Ne/Nc ratio](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Ne\_Nc-ratio.html)

name: species_related
label::English (en): What closely related/highly similar species is the ratio based on?
hint::English (en): Please write the scientific name.

name: ratio_species_related
label::English (en): If yes (at the species level), please provide the ratio.
hint::English (en): Use decimals (".") instead of "/". NOTE: A single value per species is recommended; however, if there is some uncertainty in this ratio, a range may be provided.

name: ratio_year
label::English (en): In what year was the ratio established (sampling, not publication)?

name: source_popsize_ratios
label::English (en): Source of ratio data (literature reference, website link, expert consultation)
hint::English (en): Please list all relevant sources used in determining the conversion ratio and provide further information if needed. If it was based on expert consultation, please provide name of expert(s).

name: species_comments
label::English (en): Any additional comments or notes regarding the information that has been provided above.

name: section5
label::English (en): Section 5: Population size data for the proportion of populations with an affective population size > 500 (Ne 500 indicator)
hint::English (en): Please provide additional information for each population

name: section5_note
label::English (en): Questions in this section are directly associated with calculating the Ne 500 indicator. This section will only appear if you stated that there is Nc or Ne data for at least one population.   Also the number of populations you will be required to answer questions is directly related to the number of EXTANT  populations that were entered in Section 3. Data for no more than 25 populations can be entered in the kobo form, but more can be added in the [text template](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/6\_Calculations\_and\_reporting/R\_scripts.html#getting-the-population-data-if-the-template-was-used)

name: kobo_tabular
label::English (en): If you have a large number of populations, would you prefer to enter them individually in the Kobo Form OR upload a spreadsheet with the required information?
hint::English (en): Only choose the upload option if you have a large number of populations.  The template provided in the Kobo Manual MUST be used.

name: pop_tabular_file
label::English (en): Please upload the .txt file following the template you can find [HERE](https://github.com/AliciaMstt/GeneticIndicators?tab=readme-ov-file#22-population-information-template)
hint::English (en): in the file name, please follow this format: country\_speciesname\_assesorname.txt Make sure to save as "tab delimited"

name: pop1
label::English (en): Population 1

name: Name_pop1
label::English (en): Population 1 name
hint::English (en): If a name has not been assigned to this population in literature, please provide your own unique name here.

name: Origin_pop1
label::English (en): What is the origin of population 1? See definitions [HERE](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#origin--of-population)
hint::English (en): You can provide details in the comments section for this population, if needed.

name: IntroductionYear_pop1

name: Ne_pop1
label::English (en): What is the effective population size (Ne) for population 1? (POINT ESTIMATE)
hint::English (en): If you have a confidence interval include it in next questions. If Ne is not known for this population, type -999
constraint_message: the Ne can't be negative, and only -999 is accepted if the Ne is not avilable (NA)

name: NeLower_pop1
label::English (en): If available, which is the lower limit of the Ne confidence interval for population 1?
hint::English (en): If not available, type -999
constraint_message: Ne lower bound can't be negative and has to be lower than Ne. Only -999 is accepted if this value is unknown (NA)

name: Did_you_mean_999_2
label::English (en): Did you mean -999 instead of 999? please change to **-999**

name: NeUpper_pop1
label::English (en): If available, which is the upper limit of the Ne confidence interval for population 1?
hint::English (en): If not available, type -999. If infinite, type 999 999 999
constraint_message: Ne upper bound can't be negative and has to be larger than Ne. Only -999 is accepted if this value is unknown (NA)
guidance_hint: If the Ne estimate is infinity please use "999,999,999" (make sure you use 9 times the number 9).

name: Did_you_mean_999_2_001
label::English (en): Did you mean -999 instead of 999? please change to **-999**

name: NeYear_pop1
label::English (en): In what year was the data used to estimate Ne collected for population 1?
hint::English (en): Please state the year when the sampling was done, not when it was published.

name: GeneticMarkers_pop1
label::English (en): What genetic markers were used to estimate Ne for THIS population? See definitions [HERE](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#genetic-markers)

name: GeneticMarkersOther_pop1
label::English (en): If 'Other', please explain.

name: MethodNe_pop1
label::English (en): What method was used in calculating Ne for THIS population?

name: SourceNe_pop1
label::English (en): Please list all relevant sources reporting on effective population size for THIS population
hint::English (en): Please separate each source using a semicolon (;).

name: transboundary_pop1
label::English (en): Is THIS population part of a transboundary population?
hint::English (en): Transboundary refers to its existence in one or more countries, moving across oceans, being migratory, etc.

name: percent_pop1
label::English (en): What percentage of THIS population is in South Africa?
hint::English (en): Please record a number between 0-100 (use whole numbers). Enter -999 if the percentage is unknown and cannot be estimated.

name: whole_or_part_pop1
label::English (en): Is the census size estimated for the population as a whole (i.e., across all transboundary countries) or only for the portion within South Africa?

name: NcType_pop1
label::English (en): Is the census population size (Nc) available as a range or point estimate? See [guidelines for details](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/3\_Howto\_guides\_examples/Populations\_sizes.html#how-to-get-the-nc)

name: NcYear_pop1
label::English (en): In what year was the Nc estimated for population 1?
hint::English (en): Please state the year when the sampling was done, not when it was published

name: NcMethod_pop1
label::English (en): How was Nc calculated in THIS population?

name: NcRange_pop1
label::English (en): Whats the range of the Nc for population 1?

name: NcRangeDetails_pop1
label::English (en): If a more detailed range is available please enter it here.

name: NcPoint_pop1
label::English (en): If known, what is the census population size (Nc) for population 1? (POINT ESTIMATE)
hint::English (en): If you have a confidence interval include it in next questions.
constraint_message: the Nc can't be negative, and only -999 is accepted if the Nc is not avilable (NA)

name: NcLower_pop1
label::English (en): If available, which is the LOWER limit of the Nc confidence interval for population 1?
hint::English (en): This should be the lower value of the 95% Confidence Interval. If that is unavailable, leave this question blank and please record the confidence interval used (e.g. 90%) in the 'ANY ADDITIONAL COMMENTS OR NOTES' question at the end of the Section.
constraint_message: the lower Nc limit can't be negative and has to be lower than the Nc. Only -999 is accepted if this value is unknown (NA)

name: NcUpper_pop1
label::English (en): If available, which is the UPPER limit of the Nc confidence interval for population 1?
hint::English (en): This should be the upper value of the 95% Confidence Interval. If that is unavailable, please record the confidence interval used (e.g. 90%) in the 'ANY ADDITIONAL COMMENTS OR NOTES' question at the end of the Section.
constraint_message: the upper Nc limit can't be negative and has to be larger than the Nc. Only -999 is accepted if this value is unknown (NA)

hint::English (en): Please separate sources using a semicolon (;)

label::English (en): This section should ONLY be completed if there is data on the number of individuals for the ENTIRE SPECIES; and SHOULD NOT be completed if individual population size data exists.

name: national_endemic
label::English (en): Is this species a national endemic?
hint::English (en): Occurs no where else other than South Africa

name: sa_percent
label::English (en): What percentage of the species occurs in South Africa?
hint::English (en): Note: Occurs refers to where the individuals breed and/or spend the majority of their time. Please record a number between 0-100. If an approximate percentage cannot be estimated, enter -999.

name: sp_whole_or_part
label::English (en): Is the census size estimated for the species as a whole (i.e., across all transboundary countries) or only for the portion within South Africa?

name: nc_type_sp
label::English (en): Is the census size available as a range or point estimate?

name: nc_range_sp
label::English (en): What is the range of Nc for the species?

name: nc_range_details_sp
label::English (en): If a more detailed range is available, please enter it here.

name: nc_point_sp
label::English (en): What is the census size (Nc) for the species? (POINT ESTIMATE)
hint::English (en): If you have a confidence interval include it in next questions. Leave blank if Nc was not quantitatively estimated.

name: nc_lower_sp
label::English (en): If available, which is the LOWER limit of the Nc confidence interval for the species?
hint::English (en): This should be the lower value of the 95% Confidence Interval. If that is unavailable, please record the confidence interval used (e.g. 90%) in the 'ANY ADDITIONAL COMMENTS OR NOTES' question at the end of the Section.

name: nc_upper_sp
label::English (en): If available, which is the UPPER limit of the Nc confidence interval for the species?
hint::English (en): This should be the upper value of the 95% Confidence Interval. If that is unavailable, please record the confidence interval used (e.g. 90%) in the 'ANY ADDITIONAL COMMENTS OR NOTES' question at the end of the Section.

name: nc_year_sp
label::English (en): In what year was Nc estimated for the species?
hint::English (en): Please state the year when the sampling was done, not when it was published

name: Nc_method_sp
label::English (en): How was Nc calculated for the species?

name: source_nc
label::English (en): Source of species census size information (literature reference, website link, expert consultation)
hint::English (en): Please list all relevant sources used in acquiring the species information separated by a semi-colon (;). It is advised that all referenced documents are saved to a species specific folder in your personal records in case further consultation is required. If information was based on expert consultation, please provide name of expert(s).

name: section6_comments
label::English (en): ANY ADDITIONAL COMMENTS OR NOTES with respect to the information provided in this Section.
hint::English (en): E.g.,  record the confidence interval used for the point estimate if not 95%.

name: section7
label::English (en): Section 7: Genetic monitoring indicator

name: section7_note
label::English (en): Questions in this section will contribute towards quantifying the genetic monitoring indicator - Number of species and populations in which genetic diversity is being monitored using DNA based methods. See [guidelines](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/2\_Theoretical\_background/DNA-based-monitoring-indicator.html) for details

name: gen_studies
label::English (en): Have genetic studies been conducted involving the species? See [guidelines](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#genetic-studies) for definitions

name: temp_gen_monitoring
label::English (en): Has temporal genetic monitoring been conducted for one or more populations of this species?
hint::English (en): A temporal comparison using at least two time points of various genetic diversity metrics for the species. See [guidelines](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#temporal-genetic-monitoring) for details

name: gen_monitoring_years
label::English (en): If yes, what years did this take place?

name: source_genetic_studies
label::English (en): Please cite all data sources for the genetic studies (literature reference, website link, expert consultation) separated by two colons (::).

name: section8
label::English (en): Section 8: Other Species Information

name: section8_note
label::English (en): While the answers to the questions in this section will not directly contribute to quantifying any of the genetic diversity indicators being investigated, they will help refine metrics, such as the Ne:Nc ratio, and provide contextual information on the type of species being assessed (e.g., threatened status, life history classifications) which could be informative to countries in their national reporting.

name: sa_endemic
label::English (en): Is the species a national endemic?
hint::English (en): If the species is extinct, was if a national endemic?

name: realm
label::English (en): Realm [see definition](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#realm)
hint::English (en): Select all that apply

name: IUCN_habitat
label::English (en): IUCN Habitat Classification [see definition](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#iucn-habitat-classification)
hint::English (en): IUCN (2012) IUCN Habitat Classification Scheme. https://www.iucnredlist.org/resources/habitat-classification-scheme. Select all that apply.

name: other_habitat
label::English (en): Other habitat data
hint::English (en): Please feel free to elaborate further on the habitat (sub-types) of the species. E.g., Wetland may be broken down further into streams/rivers, and lakes,. Beaches fall under  Marine Intertidal.

name: species_range
label::English (en): Species Range [see definitions](https://ccgenetics.github.io/guidelines-genetic-diversity-indicators/docs/7\_Glossary/Glossary.html#species-range)
hint::English (en): Wide-ranging: an EOO greater than 20 000 km2 (based on IUCN Criterion B1) or present in more than one-third of a country's 20-km grid squares (following Katayama et al. 2014 PLoSOne study).   Restricted: an EOO < 20 000 km2 or an AOO < 2 000 km2. A list of restricted species compiled using KBA criteria (i.e.IUCN Criteria B2) can be found online from https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/working-with-kbas/proposing-updating/criteria-tools; however, it is recognized that not all restricted species will be included in this list.

name: rarity

hint::English (en): Rare: Low densities of individuals: Species always occurs as single individuals or very small subpopulations (typically fewer than 50 mature individuals) scattered over a wide area
